## Purpose

The previous analysis (`04_differential_analysis.Rmd`, thesis) compared
KRAS- and EGFR-mutant lung lines with the other lung lines in two ways: against
all lung lines, and against a cohort filtered by co-mutations (TP53 mutant;
other driver, CDKN2A and STK11 wild type). This test redoes these four
contrasts with the current data and mutation status, puts each next to a
covariate-adjusted version that keeps all lines, and adds a direct KRAS vs EGFR
comparison.

**Decision supported:** whether exclusion by co-mutation (previous approach) or
adjustment for co-mutations (current approach) is used for lung genotype
contrasts, and whether KRAS vs EGFR is worth pursuing.

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds`
- `analyses/cancer-cell-lines/04_differential_analysis.Rmd` (previous contrasts, for the cohort definitions)
- `config.yml`: `contrast`

## Methods

Lines: lung lines used in models. Status as in the main analysis (D19, D25,
D27), with one exception for EGFR. DepMap's driver flags miss the classic
EGFR exon 19 deletions (PC9 and NCIH1650 carry E746_A750del). Activating EGFR
mutations are "small, in-frame deletions or amino acid substitutions clustered
around the ATP-binding pocket of the tyrosine kinase domain" (Lynch TJ et al.
*N Engl J Med* 2004. doi:10.1056/nejmoa040938, PMID 15118073). Here EGFR
counts as mutated with a likely-driver variant or an in-frame deletion
starting in codons 745–753 (exon 19). The general rule for oncogenes is
examined in audit/11.

Differences to the previous analysis: lines instead of injections, the log2
half-minimum transform (D7) instead of dropping ions with values <= 0, DepMap
instead of Cellosaurus status, and culture batch in every model. Each contrast
was fitted with limma on all ions; BH over all ions within each contrast.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/mutations.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/differential.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
output_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_09_previous_lung_contrasts")

data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
```

## 1. Lung lines and status

```{r status}
lung <- data$lines %>% filter(in_models, tissue == "Lung") %>% select(line, tissue, batch)
for (g in c("KRAS", "TP53", "CDKN2A", "STK11")) lung[[g]] <- altered_status(data, lung$line, g, config)

# EGFR: likely driver or in-frame exon 19 deletion (codons 745-753)
egfr <- alteration_status(data, lung$line, "EGFR") %>%
    mutate(exon19_deletion = grepl("p\\.[A-Z]7(4[5-9]|5[0-3])_[A-Z][0-9]+(del|delins)", protein_changes))
lung$EGFR <- (egfr$likely_driver | egfr$exon19_deletion)[match(lung$line, egfr$line)]
egfr %>% filter(any_mutation) %>% select(line, protein_changes, likely_driver, exon19_deletion)

# CDKN2A is unknown for lines without copy number (D27)
c(lung_lines = nrow(lung), CDKN2A_unknown = sum(is.na(lung$CDKN2A)))
lung %>% summarise(across(c(KRAS, EGFR, TP53, CDKN2A, STK11), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
preview_table(lung, caption = "Lung lines with status")
```

## 2. Contrasts

```{r contrasts}
# each contrast: lines (a filter on the lung table), group column, covariates
specs <- list(
    KRAS_all = list(lines = quote(TRUE), group = "KRAS", covariates = character()),
    KRAS_filtered = list(lines = quote(TP53 & !EGFR & !CDKN2A & !STK11), group = "KRAS", covariates = character()),
    KRAS_adjusted = list(lines = quote(TRUE), group = "KRAS", covariates = c("TP53", "EGFR", "CDKN2A", "STK11")),
    EGFR_all = list(lines = quote(TRUE), group = "EGFR", covariates = character()),
    EGFR_filtered = list(lines = quote(TP53 & !KRAS & !CDKN2A & !STK11), group = "EGFR", covariates = character()),
    EGFR_adjusted = list(lines = quote(TRUE), group = "EGFR", covariates = c("TP53", "KRAS", "CDKN2A", "STK11")),
    KRAS_vs_EGFR = list(lines = quote(KRAS | EGFR), group = "KRAS", covariates = character())
)

run_spec <- function(spec) {
    d <- lung %>%
        filter(!is.na(.data[[spec$group]])) %>%
        filter(if_all(all_of(spec$covariates), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
        filter(coalesce(!!spec$lines, FALSE))
    d$group <- d[[spec$group]]
    X <- contrast_design(d, spec$covariates)
    fit <- fit_contrast(data, d, X)
    list(d = d, X = X, table = fit$table)
}
results <- lapply(specs, run_spec)

summary_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(results), function(id) {
    r <- results[[id]]
    tibble(contrast = id, lines = nrow(r$d), mutant = sum(r$d$group), other = sum(!r$d$group),
           batches_of_mutant = n_distinct(r$d$batch[r$d$group]),
           residual_df = nrow(r$X) - ncol(r$X),
           p_below_0.05 = sum(r$table$P.Value < 0.05),
           adj_p_below_0.05 = sum(r$table$adj.P.Val < 0.05),
           min_adj_p = min(r$table$adj.P.Val),
           null_share = round(limma::propTrueNull(r$table$P.Value), 2))
}))
summary_table
```

In the KRAS vs EGFR contrast, "mutant" is the KRAS group and "other" the EGFR
group. The null share is limma's estimate of the share of ions without an
effect; 55 ions with p < 0.05 are expected by chance.

## 3. Exclusion vs adjustment

```{r agreement, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
# t-statistics of the filtered and the adjusted version against the "all" version
compare <- function(gene) {
    t_of <- function(id) select(results[[id]]$table, feature_id, t) %>% rename(!!id := t)
    t_of(paste0(gene, "_all")) %>%
        inner_join(t_of(paste0(gene, "_filtered")), by = "feature_id") %>%
        inner_join(t_of(paste0(gene, "_adjusted")), by = "feature_id") %>%
        rename_with(~ sub(paste0(gene, "_"), "", .x)) %>%
        mutate(gene = gene)
}
t_values <- bind_rows(compare("KRAS"), compare("EGFR"))
t_values %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(filtered_vs_all = cor(filtered, all, method = "spearman"),
              adjusted_vs_all = cor(adjusted, all, method = "spearman"),
              filtered_vs_adjusted = cor(filtered, adjusted, method = "spearman"))

p <- t_values %>%
    pivot_longer(c(filtered, adjusted), names_to = "version", values_to = "t_version") %>%
    ggplot(aes(all, t_version)) +
    geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.6) +
    facet_grid(version ~ gene) +
    labs(x = "t, all lung lines", y = "t, filtered / adjusted",
         title = "Exclusion-based and covariate-adjusted versions vs all lung lines") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "versions", output_dir, width = 8, height = 4)
p
```

## 4. Top ions

```{r top}
bind_rows(lapply(names(results), function(id) mutate(results[[id]]$table, contrast = id))) %>%
    group_by(contrast) %>%
    slice_min(P.Value, n = 5) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(contrast, name = substr(name, 1, 50), logFC = round(logFC, 2), P.Value, adj.P.Val) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Five strongest ions per contrast")
```

## Interpretation

- **The co-mutation filter removes most lines.** The KRAS cohort shrinks from
  85 to 24 lines (7 KRAS-mutant), and the EGFR cohort from 85 to 18 lines
  with a **single** EGFR-mutant line (NCIH3255).
- **With one mutant line the test turns into an outlier test.** EGFR_filtered
  is the only contrast with ions at adjusted p < 0.05 (10-nitrolinoleic acid,
  adjusted p 4 × 10⁻⁶; pantothenic acid, log2FC −7). In NCIH3255, both ions
  have negative raw intensities, so they sit at the half-minimum floor (D7).
  These "hits" are imputation values in one line, not EGFR effects. The same
  ion leads KRAS_vs_EGFR (+4.2).
- **Filtering changes the result; adjusting does not.** The filtered versions
  correlate only moderately with the all-lines versions (Spearman 0.54 KRAS,
  0.42 EGFR), while the covariate-adjusted versions keep the pattern
  (0.89, 0.91) and all lines (76; 9 lines without CDKN2A copy number drop
  out, D27).
- **No version has a reliable ion-level effect** for KRAS or EGFR in lung
  (smallest adjusted p ≥ 0.58 apart from the artefact above). With four EGFR
  lines from two batches, KRAS vs EGFR (25 vs 4) has little power.

**Conclusion:** the exclusion-based design of the previous analysis is not
kept; lung genotype contrasts adjust for co-mutations instead (as D18/D22).
Small groups need a guard against effects carried by imputed values:
exploratory results should report, per ion, how many values of the smaller
group are imputed.
